title: The GPU Shortage Inside Your Own Infrastructure: Why AI Workloads Queue While Capacity Sits Idle
slides: Your GPUs sit idle while AI jobs queue. Why?
Schedulers treat AI like batch jobs, not compute-hungry tenants
But the bottleneck isn't hardware—it's resource fragmentation
Reclaim stranded GPU memory with smarter bin-packing today
Audit your scheduler before buying another GPU
thread_text:
1. Your GPUs Are Waiting

Your AI jobs don't run because the hardware is broken. They queue because schedulers treat them like batch jobs, leaving compute stranded.

2. Schedulers Are the Problem

AI workloads need continuous compute, not batch slots. Legacy schedulers kill utilization by design.

3. Fragmentation Kills More Than Hardware

You don't need more GPUs. You need smarter bin-packing to reclaim stranded memory across nodes.

4. Reclaim Stranded Memory Now

Bin-packing reallocates idle GPU memory without new hardware. Audit your current utilization today.

5. Audit Before You Buy

Check your scheduler's fragmentation rate before your next GPU purchase. If it's above 20%, fix that first.

Your AI jobs are stuck in a queue while the graphics chips you already pay for sit at half capacity.

It's not a hardware failure. Schedulers still treat AI tasks like batch jobs, so compute gets stranded across nodes.

The real problem is fragmentation, not a shortage: memory sits idle on one machine while jobs wait on another.

If you build or ship anything with AI, smarter bin-packing can reclaim that memory without buying a single new card. 🔧

Check your scheduler's fragmentation rate before your next purchase. If it's above 20%, fix that first. 📊
